annotations.title: A man that is an Heretike.
annotations.text: [1] Not euery one that erreth in religion, is an Heretike, but he onely that after the Churches determination, wilfully and ſtubburnely ſtandeth in his falſe opinion, not yelding to decree of Councel or the cheefe Paſtors of the Church therein. They (ſaith S. Auguſtine ep. 162.) that defend their ſentence (though falſe and peruerſe) with no ſtubburne ſtomake or obſtinate hart, ſpecially if it be ſuch as them ſelues by bold preſumption broched not, but receiued it of their deceiued parents, and do ſeeke the truth vvarily and carefully, being ready to be reformed if they finde it, ſuch are not to be reputed among Heretikes. And againe, li. 18 de Ciuit. c. 51. [2] They that in the Church of Chriſt haue any craſed or peruerſe opinion, if being admoniſhed to be of a ſound and right opinion, they reſiſt obſtinatly, and vvil not amend their peſtiferous opinions, but perſiſt in defenſe of them, are thereby become Heretikes, and going forth out of the Church, are counted for enimies that exerciſe vs. Againe li. 4 de Bapt. cont. Donat. c. 16. He is an Heretike that, when the doctrine of the Catholike faith is made plaine and manifeſt vnto him, had rather reſiſt it, and chooſe that vvhich him ſelf held &c. And in diuers places he declareth that S. Cyprian, though he held an errour, yet vvas no Heretike, becauſe he vvould not haue defended it after a general Council had declared it to be an errour. li. 2 de bapt. c. 4. So Poſſidonius in the life of S. Auguſtine [3] reporteth, how, after the determination of the See Apoſtolike that Pelagius opinion vvas heretical, al men eſteemed Pelagius an Heretike, and the Emperour made lavves againſt him as againſt an Heretike. Againe S. Auguſtine ſaith, He is an Heretike in my opinion, that for ſome temporal commoditie, and ſpecially for his glorie and principalitie, coineth or els foloweth falſe or new opinions. de vtilit. credendi cap. 1. [4] Let our Proteſtants behold them ſelues in this glaſſe, and vvithal let them marke al other proprieties that old Heretikes euer had, and they ſhal finde al definitions and markes of an Heretike to fall vpon them ſelues. And therfore they muſt not maruel if vve warne al Catholike men by the vvordes of the Apoſtle in this place, to take heede of them, and to ſhunne their preachings, bookes, conuenticles and companies. [5] Neither neede the people be curious to knowe what they ſay, much leſſe to confute them: but they muſt truſt Gods Church, which doth refute and condemne them. And it is ynough for them to knowe that they be condemned, as S Auguſtine noteth in the later end of his booke de hereſibus. And S. Cyprian [6] ſaith notably to Antonianus demaunding curiouſly vvhat hereſies Nouatianus did teach: No matter, quoth he, What hereſies he hath or teacheth, when he teacheth vvithout, that is to ſay, out of the Church.

annotations.title: Subuerted.
annotations.text: ◦ Heretikes are often incorrigible, yet the Church of God ceaſeth not by al meanes poſſible to reuoke them. therfore S. Auguſtine ſaith ep. 162. The Heretike him ſelf though ſwelling with odious and deteſtable pride, and madde vvith the frovvardnes of wicked contention, as We admoniſh that he be auoided leſt he deceiue the vveaklings and litle ones, ſo we refuse not by al meanes poſſible to ſeeke his amendment and reformation.

notes.text: The Church seeketh the amendement of the most obstinate Heretikes.

annotations.title: By his owne iudgement.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Other greuous offenders be ſeparated by excommunication from the communion of Saincts and the fellowſhip of Gods Church, by the ſentence of their Superiors in the ſame Church: but Heretikes more miſerable and infortunate then they, runne out of the Church of their ovvne accord, and ſo giue ſentence againſt their ovvne ſoules to damnation.

notes.text: Heretikes cut them selues frō the Church.
